doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

chapter: Social life of old New Orleans
title: Women in ballrooms and barrooms
summary: Speakers say trouble began once ladies were admitted to the ballroom and barroom.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Oh, I'd wag them too. I may say one thing that you all may not think is right. I'm going to say one thing. Just the minute that they let the ladies go into the ballroom and everything, that's part of everything. Everything. The kids couldn't be, you had to be 21 to be into the nightclub. You have to be 21. But you see? See? But, let the ladies go into the ballroom, then things commence to get real rough.

You see? See, there's other words, the ladies, but I don't think no ladies should be, sir, I don't drink to no men's. I think men's ballroom should be for them. If a man got his wife, you got two departments. Take your wife in the department where it is and let the hobos be by themselves, that's right?
Well, he's right. Well, that was small. The ladies' folks couldn't go to the barroom. You think about that?

No, I just beat my wife in the... They couldn't go, no, minors couldn't go in the barroom. No, man. They couldn't go, man. They couldn't go, man. You couldn't go, man. You couldn't go, man. You couldn't go, man. You couldn't go, man. That's right. You can't be in the ballroom. And at that time, when they couldn't go in the ballroom, they had so many parties and dancers here, go over there. They didn't go in there. They didn't go in there. Why? Because you cannot go in the ballroom. They have to go there. Now, everything is in the ballroom. Everything is in there. And that's why all the hell is in there.
